I've used dozens of water bottles over the years and there's always been a problem: one is too big so it doesn't fit in my purse or water bottle pocket on my backpack, another leaks like nobody's business, another has a straw that just won't stay attached so you're sipping air most of the time, and others just don't lock up nice and tight.

One day, I was talking with my sister over lunch and I had noticed she pulled this water bottle from the dark recesses of her tote and nothing in her purse was wet. I was impressed. She had gotten this water bottle when she bought a 4 years ago and had used this water bottle exclusively since. She took it with her abroad and takes it to college classes everyday with no problems. After I hear her rave reviews, I decided to buy one.

I've been using this water bottle for a few months now and I honestly am in love. The slim design makes it unique compared to the typical Nalgene but it still feels very sturdy. Not quite a liter of water but it's more than the typically grocery story water bottle. The loop on the top makes it easy to grab on the go and even hook, via carabiner, to a strap or your bag. My favorite feature is the locking mouth piece.

In order to drink water, you have to flip the metal lock down and push the button to pop the lid off. I've read some reviews saying that this is too much effort but honestly, I love it. I know that the water bottle won't leak and it hasn't. I work in a school and I carry this around all day. Sometimes my students accidentally kick it across the floor and no water ever leaks. No twisting off lids: just flip the lock down, press the button and delicious H2O is delivered to your mouth with no spills.

Bottom line: buy this water bottle. I love it and I think you will too.

text_fidelity_a:
HOZAN Spoke Threading Machine C700 This tool gets a bad rap, and unfairly, I think. Sure it takes time, but it works fine for the occasional wheel building project or replacement spoke. It's a nice item to have in the tool box for a rainy day when you can't be riding. You can build or repair a wheel instead. Even a bike shop might find one of these handy.

It's fairly simple. The tool mounts in a vise. The three rollers emboss threads in the spoke, rather than cut them. This makes for a stronger spoke. You turn the crank and the rollers "chase" threads up the spoke. When you get the threaded length you want, you turn the crank in reverse to back the rollers off the spoke.

I just used it to thread 36 14-gauge spokes, with no problems at all. (It threads 14 and 15 gauge spokes.)

The keys to using this tool successfully are to generously use cutting oil (or an equivalent), start with a properly chamfered spoke, and make several passes to get the depth of thread you want.

I think one reason this device gets such a bad rap is that people try to make it cut finished threads in one pass. If you tighten down the rollers that much to start, it will be difficult to get a blank spoke to feed into them.

Practice with a few extra spokes first. Chamfer the ends slightly with a file or a grinder.

Open up the Hozan tool's rollers by loosening the adjustment nut, until it will easily "take" a blank spoke and lightly emboss threads. Back the spoke out, tighten the nut a quarter to half turn, and make another pass through. Repeat this until you get threads embossed deeply enough so that a spoke nipple screws on easily for its full length. That will be your final setting.

Now you can back the adjustment nut off a full turn (360 degrees). This is so you can start a blank spoke. Make a first pass through, back the spoke out, tighten the adjustment nut a half turn, pass the spoke through and back out, and tighten it one half turn again for the final pass. Repeat this process for every spoke you want to thread. After a few you'll get into a rhythm and things will go faster. Apply more cutting oil with every spoke.

After every few spokes clean the rollers. I spray them with WD-40 while holding a folded paper towel underneath, then re-oil them for the next spoke.

The instructions say that with proper care this tool will last for years. I don't see any reason why it won't.
text_fidelity_b: HOZAN Spoke Threading Machine C700

Meditation bench, Seiza Bench,It's Adjustable, Portable,Lightweight and Durable I'm over 60, and wanted to learn to sit seiza again; however sharp pains in my calfs and ankles made it difficult to maintain. I figured I could work up to it with this little bench, and it's doing the trick!! I gradually lowered the height to the lowest level...then I took a 7/8" diameter dowel and some scrap wood, and made a substitute "T" to fit under the seat. As my comfort with a height increases, I take the dowel and saw off about 1/4" at a time to reduce the height a bit. I'm finally able to sit seiza, even without the bench, without serious pain; I'll continue to lower the height and practice daily until I don't need the bench at all, but in the meantime, it makes sitting seiza for extended periods much more comfortable.

As others have noted, the bench has little padding (just a thin layer of dense foam), so this may not be comfortable if you're carrying much excess weight, since that would increase the pressure on your thighs. Since it looks like free returns aren't offered, you might consider buying a used bench (if available) to try it out less expensively; it's very sturdy, so a used one should work fine.

text_fidelity_a:
FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player I bought this primarily to listen to Podcasts and some music while swimming laps. When it arrived, I was pleased with the hardware quality and ease of use. I loaded up some music and Podcasts and headed for the pool. It was relatively easy to clip the units to my goggles. The controls could be better, but are not terrible. I put it on, started playing a Podcast, put in my earplugs and started swimming. I had been concerned that my goggles might leak or come off during turns with these units clipped on, but it was not a problem at all.
The problem, though, was the sound. If sitting perfectly still underwater, it sounds decent. Pretty much on par with my 30-year-old one-speaker clock radio. However, even with earplugs, the noise of swimming and rushing water overpowers it. If I play familiar songs I can tell what I am listening to and somewhat enjoy them. However, forget about the spoken word. I had to turn the volume up really loud to be able to make out most of what was said on the Podcast due to distortion and background noise. And then it was just too loud to be enjoyable. In fact, I am sure that others in the pool could hear some sound from it. I tried to adjust it in every possible way, and followed the instructions precisely.
This seems like a good idea, but I am disappointed, especially for the cost.

Pros: Solid design, no earphones or earbuds, can still wear earplugs, easy to wear, stays on goggles and doesn't pull them off, easy to load songs.
Cons: Price, 1 GB of storage is a total insult, limited features and controls for an MP3 player, poor sound quality overshadows all else.
text_fidelity_b: FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player

Sven-Saw 60th Anniversary Engraved 21" Folding Saw I bought this to replace a Corona folding saw in my off-road SUV. I use this saw primarily to clear branches that block the trail or to cut up trees or limbs that have fallen across the trail and are too big to pull clear. Even if I use the winch, some things need to but cut up so they will fit into where I want to pull them. I don't have room to always carry a gas-powered chainsaw, but a fast hand saw works great for wet wood up to 6 inches and dry (dead) wood possibly 8 to 10 inches thick. Bigger than that, I probably don't need to bother it.

My biggest reason for replacing the folding saw was that the particular one I had didn't sheild all the teeth of the curved blade within the wood handle. I didn't like the sharp saw teeth in my tool bag. A straight saw (with the handle in a straight line from the blade) doesn't give the best power, but this triangular design is the best of both worlds (folds straight, and opens to a large angle between the blade and handle).

The disadvantage of a frame saw like this is that you can run into the limit of the frame cutting through a thick piece. A panel saw (whether fixed or folding handle) can keep going indefinitely. Still, there are some practical limits imposed by how hard I want to work and how thick a piece is going to be while still being narrow enough that my saw length will span it. I feel confident the 21" frame saw will meet my needs. While a considerably smaller panel saw with no frame in the way would also do very well, the folding design of the Sven's frame is such that it has the advantage in compactness. The length won't fit in a tool bag, but the very thin design fits neatly under the rear bench seat in my SUV along with my other long tools (a 48" Hi-Lift bar and handle, an 18" socket handle, and spare 5/8 wave VHF antenna).

I added a washer between the wing-nut and saw handle. This provides a bearing surface for the wing nut which does not turn against the Aluminum handle.
text_fidelity_b: Sven-Saw 60th Anniversary Engraved 21" Folding Saw

Now for review. I bought this for my Century Arms  CANiK TP9SA. It did not fit completely snug due to where my trigger guard and accessory notches on my pistol frame correspond, my TP9SA just doesn't fit "perfectly" with this light. I have three notches on my TP9SA rail. The flashlight will sit in the first notch, but does not stream the light in a straight, parallel trajectory. If you have (glove size) large hands, you can operate the switch with minimal effort using your index finger. + You have to engage the on/off switch twice to activate the strobe setting. A minor irritant and engineering flaw. Other than that, light shines bright, strobe will give you a seizure. Seems pretty durable. I haven't shot with it yet to test durability. text_fidelity_a:
AXV Vibration Plate Exercise Machine Whole Body Workout Vibrate Fitness Platform Lymphatic Drainage Machine for Weight Loss Shaping Toning Wellness Home Gyms Workout I've wanted one of these vibration platforms for a long time, after reading a book on Whole Body Vibration (WBV) for seniors. That book said not to get an oscillation machine, which this is, because the oscillations can cause injuries that the more expensive machine types don't, but this one is so small I find I'm having no difficulty at all with the oscillations. Put it this way: I could never afford a more expensive machine, and the fact that I was offered this on Vine for review is what made me able to try a WBV platform at all.

This smaller model does not have bluetooth, unlike some of the larger vibration plates offered on AXV's sales page, but that's just fine with me. I wanted something inexpensive and uncomplicated that I can keep by my bed and stand on while watching TV. As my room is arranged, it turns out that my recliner is perfectly positioned to hold onto while I'm standing on the platform for extra stability, and it can sit unobtrusively by the head of my bed so I'm always reminded to use it. I don't even have to stow it away.

The manual that came with this mini vibration plate was plenty detailed in terms of what you can do with this, but it does not have clear explanations of what the different programmed settings do, which I think they should add. Because of my age and the fact that I have osteoporosis, I'm not likely to try the exercises included in the manual except for maybe the biceps curls and calf raises, but these are clearly shown in photographs if you're interested.

When I saw in the answers to customer questions that this machine is manufactured at the same factory as another well-known product, I went to good old YouTube and searched for videos for help. I found "Waver Mini Vibration Platform Orientation" and it looks almost exactly like this product in terms of size and shape. After watching that video, which had a wealth of information about how to use the different programs along with cautionary info for beginners, I'm thinking this machine's programs are set up in a similar way so the advice for the Waver likely applies to this machine as well.

Unlike some of the other WBV machines offered by AXV, this mini has nine programs. I didn't run through all of them, but from trying P0 through P4 and then running a few of the higher programs without standing on the platform, it appears that these programs do coincide with the Waver programs in terms of intensity: first third beginning level, second third intermediate, final third advanced. When a program is running, the selected program number is shown on the left and "14" on the right, which I think means it starts out on a 14 intensity setting out of 99. The P# screen cycles between the program and a from-10-minute countdown number that, when you're in your last minute of WBV, switches to seconds remaining. I found this very helpful.

The only thing I didn't like, and why I knocked off a star, is that the carbiner clips you use to affix the resistance bands kept coming off, probably because they're pretty cheap. I'll probably buy some stainless steel locking ones to be sure the bands don't snap off while I'm using them, because the two times it happened it destabilized my balance and I almost fell. Not a good thing for someone with osteoporosis! Other than that, I think this is a fine value for someone wanting to try a vibration platform, and I think it's just right for seniors. Just make sure you don't weigh over 264 lbs. and, if you do, get a machine rated higher.
text_fidelity_b: AXV Vibration Plate Exercise Machine Whole Body Workout Vibrate Fitness Platform Lymphatic Drainage Machine for Weight Loss Shaping Toning Wellness Home Gyms Workout

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Essentials Women's Studio Sculpt Mid-Rise Capri Yoga Legging I usually size up a little for yoga/fitness pants, since I am a large medium/small large. These are sized as expected, but if you're like I am (between sizes), go up for more comfort, or go down for more compression and tummy support--either should work fine, depending on your preferences.

The fabric is opaque, so that's excellent--no see through stuff, so you can do your poses without worrying about that.

The problem I have is this: the band on the waist is placed and fitted in such a way to almost emphasize a belly roll. I'm meaty but athletic, and my tummy is relatively flat because my skin is still tight and I have a lot of muscle underneath my extra padding (I love food, and exercise is a way to let me eat, not to try and be skinny. I just don't care about that at all, really!). Most pants don't result in a bulge at my lower abdomen. None of them, really, unless the waistband is high and too tight. With these, it almost creates a pocket, where the top and bottom of the band are both quite tight compared to the middle un-seamed section with two layers of fabric. Those two layers are not really doing their job, so you end up with this loose middle section right at the crest of the lower belly. What's that do? It creates a small doughnut of skin. Not a look I am going for, and probably not one you are either. These pants are weird--I own like a million leggings. It's basically what I wear all the time. These are the only ones that really do this. I dunno...not the best design, and the sculpting is NOT what you want!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Essentials Women's Studio Sculpt Mid-Rise Capri Yoga Legging

Coleman Company Signature Instant Cabin 10 Person Classic Tent, Black/Grey UPDATE Feb 2018: We've used this tent a lot in the last couple years. I started out really liking it except for a few little things. But now, the more I use it, the more I hate it. The primary cause of that is the door zippers. They are a major pain to zip and unzip, constantly getting stuck. It just ruins the whole peacefulness of camping when you're fighting a stupid zipper. Next is the bag. One of the seams has completely ripped making the bag almost useless, and the tent really needs a bag, even if it's flimsy crappy quality like what it comes with. Dropping from 4 to 3 stars.

Have used this tent 3 times now for camping. Overall, we really like the tent, but there are a few cons...

1. This is a big footprint - 10' x 14'. Where we camp - in the Sierra's mostly - it's not always easy to find that big of a spot that is level. And you DO want it level. For one, you need to sleep on level ground. Two, the legs won't adjust very well to unlevel ground which makes the tent lean and be unstable.

2. Thought we would like the idea of the "hinged" door, but honestly it's just a pain. It comes with 2 fiberglass poles that fit into hard plastic cups in the door. The poles have rubberized tips to keep them from poking through the cups, but they inevitable get stuck in the cups and pull off the poles. Then they poke holes into the cups making the whole system useless. The long pole that goes around the rim is a real pain to bend into position. Then, once the whole thing is installed, the door doesn't fit well when closed. Kinda hangs at a wierd angle leaving gaps in the doorway so that bugs and critters can get in. So basically we ditched the poles and just use the door like a regular tent and zip/unzip whenever we go in or out. Leading to the next issue...

3. The zippers are not high quality and frequently get jammed up. Not fun anytime, but especially not in the middle of the night.

4. The storage bag, which we think is pretty essential, is junk. Very thin and flimsy material with lousy stitching. Ours split a seam on the first repacking. The material is so thin that it's probably useless to try and restitch it. We'll probably re-purpose one of our old military duffel bags as a new bag. Not ideal.

5. Kinda nitpicky, but there aren't any loops or hooks for hanging lanterns or anything else. Seems like an oversight.

6. Sloping sides makes it awkward to move around a queen mattress it you have it in the middle. Fortunately, there's two doors, one on each end.

What we like about it:

1. Super easy to set up and tear down. My wife and I can have this up/down in about 5 minutes, and I can do it myself easily. Just take a little time and make sure the legs are positioned correctly. There is no need to force anything, so if you're trying to force something, you're doing it wrong. However, there is no indication on the tent when folded that indicates where the main door is. When you've set it up once - use a sharpie on the top pole hub to indicate the direction of the front door so you can point it in that direction when setting it up. Again, it helps to have level ground so the legs don't get kinked in any weird directions. Watch setup videos a few times so you have it imprinted what it should look like.

2. The space is great. Just right for the two of us! We have plenty of room for a queen air mattress and separate spaces for each of our stuff. So far, we haven't found a big enough flat spot to give us flexibility in where we put the mattress (except in the backyard), so we haven't settled on the ideal mattress placement.

3. Love the top screen for star gazing in bed and all the windows.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Company Signature Instant Cabin 10 Person Classic Tent, Black/Grey

I'm now down to 1 star and feeling disappointed for trying to support a lesser-known American brand. I should've just gone with a more affordable option like Walmart for a no-name towel....

At the time I received my towels I didn't notice they were two different styles, we didn't unpackage them and they came in identical carry sacks. I realized when we used them together this weekend they are different. His towel has rounded edges and a soft fabric tag. My towel set has a cheaper-feeling paper tag and square edges. Again, these aren't make-or-break issues for a camp towel but I literally bought two of the SAME THING at the SAME time - it's not like I bought one last year and a newer style replaced the old one. Why couldn't you just send me two of the same thing? And why do none of the photos show a rounded edged towel?

UGHHHH. I've come away feeling like this company is not all it's cracked up to be and the products are misrepresented. It's a shame!!! I repped Wise Owl hard and bragged to many of my climbing/outdoorsy friends that I found an affordable and cool start-up. I've purchased Wise Owl towels, a camp pillow, a camp blanket, and was gifted their hammock. I feel like I know the products well and I'm sad to say I won't recommend some of them.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I'm an avid camper and climber. I found out about Wise Owl after receiving a hammock as a gift (it's awesome btw). I decided to try these towels to save some space in our packs (my partner and I have been lugging around standard bath towels). I purchased the Red set in XL and gifted him the Marine Blue set in XL. text_fidelity_a:
Universal E40 Elliptical (Discontinued) Wow! First of all the shipping box is very heavy! Thank goodness for shipping straps and a dolly.
Putting it together may look complicated but, the instructions are very well written and it does have great illustrations.
It does supply a couple of wrenches. I prefer my own tools that made it easier.
Make sure you have a large area to work in. Makes it easier to spread things out so you can see everything easily.
It took me about 3 hours to build with the help of my wife. She's better with illustrations, I'm better with written directions.
Make sure you tighten all fasteners!
Like that it has a platform for my tablet and it also has built in speakers.
The E40 Eliptical Machine has 7 different workout programs which makes working out different for each day of the week if I want.
Has readouts for time, rpm, distance, pulse, speed, calories, resistance level, and course profile.
Using this machine is easy. It's so nice and quiet also which is a plus because I have it in my living room. I have about a 6x6 area for it.
After a few days of using this, my wife and I are truly enjoying this! Has moving arms so we are both getting a full workout right in the comfort of our own home.
Right now we can only handle the lowest resistance setting but, will build up to using all 8 in time.
A great machine for home use!
My only con is that it didn't come with an ac adaptor! Will have to purchase one so we don't have to rely on batteries.
The only thing good about the batteries is if you have to have this in an area where there's no outlet.
A great eliptical machine that will hopefully get us back into shape again.
text_fidelity_b: Universal E40 Elliptical (Discontinued)

text_fidelity_a:
Midkawe Punching Bag with Stand for Adults & Kids, Adjustable Height Free Standing Boxing Reflex Bag, Ideal for MMA Reflex Speed Training, Fitness,Punching and Muscle Building Great purchase! Delivered with no damage and all parts accounted for. Assembly instructions were clear and easy to follow. They provided tools that will work but I used own. Easy to assemble, took less than 10 minutes. All the parts fit together easily, and seem very well made.

The base is very heavy when filled with water. It also has suction cups on the bottom that work very well on the smooth concrete surface of my garage. In fact too well. It makes moving it around a challenge, but on the plus side it dies not move at all no matter how hard I punch or kick it. Thinking about removing the suction cups because the base is so heavy when filled with water don't think it will move.

The spring is responsive and can handle some pretty hard hits or kicks without the shaft/bag hitting the floor. It's response time to return upright isn't too bad, just don't expect to rapid speed punch if you're going to really hit hard.

The red bag itself is super dense foam, not a leather covered inflatable bag as I've seen on others. It takes quite a pounding and it feels more natural than hitting a leather covered balloon. I've hit it without gloves no issues, but longer workouts need gloves.

The height is adjustable. I'm about 6ft tall, my son is about 5ft tall, and it easily accommodates our heights. A big plus. It's easy to adjust too, and locks in place very securely and stays locked throughout use.

Overall it is a great product and good value for what you pay. Well made, high quality feel that seems it will take a beating and last. Highly satisfied. Would recommend to a friend or family.

One suggestion: after assembly and initial couple of uses, retighten all the fasteners. Initial use may slightly loosen them. After the retighten they'll stay locked in place. I haven't had any issues with things loosening after the first couple of uses.

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Maxfield Backpacking Tent, Lightweight 2-Person Tent for Camping and Hiking Honestly this tent is great, especially at the sale price it periodically goes down to. It is literally lighter than my previous 1-person tent. The stakes it comes with are great which is rare, plenty of guy-lines already attached and coiled up at the tie-off points, no issues with ventilation or heat retention in the 3-seasons it is designed for. The rainfly, footprint, and base of the tent all clip together quite nicely and have adjustment sliders to keep them correctly tensioned. The single piece pole assembly is a little counter-intuitive, but it works great once you orient it.

HOWEVER: get the footprint for it.

I bring a scrap of tarp to throw under the footprints of all my tents anyways, because a sharp, half buried rock can always ruin things, but you don't need to. A significant amount of the versatility and convenience goes away without the footprint that is designed for it, like the ability to throw the footprint and rainfly together as an emergency shelter in a few moments, or use it in an ultralight configuration to save even more weight.
The only potential concern i have is that with how light this material is, I don't know what long term durability will be. It is VERY light material, and that usually trades out durability. Time will tell.
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Maxfield Backpacking Tent, Lightweight 2-Person Tent for Camping and Hiking

text_fidelity_a: Carson FlashShield Kill Flash ARD Anti-Reflective Lens Device (BX-42),Black For $13 for 2 of these, they can't be beat.  I did read the item description that said they fit up to 43mm, but I took a chance that they would fit on my 44mm rifle scopes objective lenses.  These are cushioned spring clips.  They are NOT super heavy duty, but they are functional.  They do fit onto a 44mm objective lens.  They could easily be knocked off in the brush, should you have to run thru any.  They do what they are supposed to do, tho.  I shined a flashlight into the unit, and I got no flashback, so I'd say it's good in sunlight.  I also intend to take a small but stout rubber band and put the rubber band over the clamps to help keep the kill flash clamps more snug onto the front of the scope objective lens.  I say again, these will come off if scraped or rubbed very hard against something.  I do believe the best flash killers are the ones that thread directly inside of the objective lenses that have internal threads.  Those options are also a lot more money.  So for the money and function, these flash killers get 5 stars for now.  If they happen to fall off under heavy recoil (I shoot 308 and 30-06), I will change my rating.
text_fidelity_b: Carson FlashShield Kill Flash ARD Anti-Reflective Lens Device (BX-42),Black

text_fidelity_a:
XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination I received this light for my Dahon folding commuter bike. Previously I was using a small rechargeable light that was more for visibility to oncoming cars than to actually see the ground.

This extra illumination of this light has made a significant difference for me when commuting at night. I used to avoid areas with low illumination. The XOSS illuminates the ground in front like a car headlight allowing me to ride in total darkness. I tilt the light so can see everything coming at me from about 20-30 feet away, which is enough time to react at my normal riding speed.

I have also used both the automatic on/off motion sensor and standard on/off modes and they each worked well.

The handlebar attachment/removal system allows me to use the XOSS as a flashlight (have done this several times) and more easily charge it. However, the attachment clip has an issue - if you tighten it onto the handlebars too much, the screw will enter a hole on the bottom of the light and restrict it from being put on or removed. Be aware...

Recommended!

(update) The bracket snapped under fairly normal usage. Maybe it was the cold weather making the plastic a bit brittle... Rather than toss the light or turn it into a flashlight, I 3D printed a replacement part. You can find it on thingiverse. Just search for "XOSS Enfitnix Bike Headlight Bracket"
text_fidelity_b: XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination

iKanzi Beach Blanket, Sandproof Waterproof Beach Mat Outdoor Picnic Blankets for Travel, Camping, Hiking (Orange+Blue) When I read the description of this product I was excited but a bit worried about what kind of quality this would be. I have 3 very rough and tumble grand kids that I have recently been taking to the parks and lakes and was uncertain if it would stand up to their antics. Boy was I surprised!!

As you can see by the product description and the pictures, that the item was quite compact which is great. But don't let the small size of the packaging fool you, the beach mat is HUGE when laid out. It will indeed hold 4-9 people easily.

The fabic is thin making it light weight, but I found it to be very durable as well. Enough that having the kids run over it, even when advised not to, it stood up very well. It is very strong for being so thin and light weight, I have no doubt this is going to hold up fantastically on our next camping trip and beach trip.

The shipping was super fast and it arrived just as we were leaving for the lake to let the kids play on the beach and in the water. I was super stoked that when we were done, the sand and dirt feel right off, NOTHING was tracked in my car. I hate trying to get sand out of my car upolstry and carpets! But one of the best features is that because it is water proof, when we got to the car it was large enough that I could put across my seats and keep my seats dry from the kids' wet clothes. I am very happy I don't have to have that wet/damp smeel permiating my car, especially in the Texas hot sun.

Also, I should mention, unless I missed it I didsn't see where it stated it came with stakes to hold it down against the wind, so I was super excited to see that they were included! Awesome bonus! We didn't need the stakes, but will certain use them in the future on our next camping trip.

Great product, great price!! Definintely worth recommending!!

Overall I would recommend this to family and friends. It is super light weight, water proof, has many great uses, I found it to be extremely durable with having no worries about it ripping or falling apart.
text_fidelity_b: iKanzi Beach Blanket, Sandproof Waterproof Beach Mat Outdoor Picnic Blankets for Travel, Camping, Hiking (Orange+Blue)

Sig Sauer BUCKMASTERS Scope- 3-12x44MM BDC It's been a while now, but products coming out of China are starting to rival top quality manufacturing elsewhere. This scope is a clear sign of that. The coating is smooth with no blemishes, the glass is properly and evenly multi-coated, the reticle is straight, and knobs give you decent feedback on the turns, and the flaps have tastefully relieved SIG logo on the inside (so when you flip them open EVERYONE can see what you working with [as if it matters] but still cool). The throw lever had some blemishes on it and wasn’t screwed all the way in. The Box it comes in is very simplistic – a good thing – with minimal packaging and waste. Even the handkerchief is a nice quality and small, not like grandma’s undies that sometimes come with other scopes. I also dig on the reticle shape which reminds me of an orthodox cross – it’s not too thin or thick, just the way you’d like it (is what she said, yeah, I know…). Also, looking inside the scope with super high lumen light reveals, dare I say, precision – something unexpected at this cost level. I think Sig’s trying to introduce these in the best light possible so as to grab market share. Well, their marketing is your win (for now at least)
But wait, what’s that thing on the side, looks like scribbles or some kind – what IS that?! Meatballs with wafting smell coming off them? Frog eyes? Female crocodile cartoon eyes peeking just above the surface of the water… Let me get closer… Nah, it’s a STAG! With tiny little red beady eyes. And deformed horns. WHO thought of this logo?! Watsamadderwidu?! It’s possible the weirdest logo I’ve ever come across – it’s like slapping flame prints on a Bentley. Iiiish…
But then again, who cars, the paint doesn’t drive the car. So with that little minus, I’d say Sig’s again a winner. BTW, remember the old Nikon Buckmaster scopes? They were totally awesome maaaaaan… But then Nikon got out of the biz, so I’m wondering if there’s any connection between Sig’s Buckmasters and the Nikon Buckmaster series. Whatever the case, I highly recommend this scope. (and if you don’t like the logo, put tape over it!)
text_fidelity_b: Sig Sauer BUCKMASTERS Scope- 3-12x44MM BDC

M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length I collect knives and hawks. There are two ways that I judge the effectiveness of any sharp tool. Number One is how it stacks up to a good machete. At this point if I could only take one blade into the wilderness, it would be a high quality machete. It has reach and a long cutting surface, is fundamental in design, and can create a large protected area around the user. In addition it cuts through things easily and doesn't typically get hung up in/on the target, unlike other implements. Number Two is judging how I would feel if I were threatened with the tool. It does look wicked, it has two effective blades, it comes sharp(!), can be swung in any direction, and is well built. It's inherent light weight will allow a lot of use before arm fatigue sets in, but it does have some negatives.

On the con side, it is short and its lightness doesn't make it feel substantial in my hand. The cutting surface is much smaller than that of a good machete and of course you can't really stab with it. It is a swinging tool that will allow an experienced fighter to step inside of the swing. Although I haven't tested it, it's hard for me to believe that it can stand up to the abuse that a large man can generate. The M48 probably wouldn't last long against a hard target (breaching doors or cutting wood or metal) but it should prove to be easy to carry and extremely effective against a soft target. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit with it. The best part of the M48 is the value. It is simply one of the most cost effective blades that I have ever bought. And darn, it just looks and feels cool!
text_fidelity_b: M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length

Withings Pulse While I am only ten days into using my Withings Pulse Ox, I am very pleased with the purchase so far. Of all the devices currently on the market, this one seemed to offer the most bang for the buck. The step, activity, and sleep tracking seem to be quite accurate. The pulse and oxygen saturation monitoring are simple and precise. Battery life seems to be superb, and integration/connectivity with my iPhone have been no problem. Both the wristband and the belt clip are well-made and comfortable. I find that it really helps to motivate me to maintain and improve my health.

If I were to provide four pieces of constructive criticism they would be:
1) Make the Pulse OX waterproof or at least very water resistant.
2) Improve the Apple Healthkit Integration. I've had some issues, not in the Withings App, but within Healthkit, with doubling of steps.

4) Allow for customization of the step and sleep goals.

Overall it has been a great little device though. Used in my "App Ecosystem" of the Withings App, WebMD, MapMyRun, and Healthkit...it is a nearly complete solution for my personal wellness goals.

text_fidelity_a:
GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing I selected this luminous key ring as an aid to attaching to my camera bag and being visible at night. I wasn’t exactly sure what to expect and I had some serious doubts about the effectiveness of this product. It turns out that it’s better than I had hoped and it works well.

The concept is very simple: expose it to bright light for a little while and it will glow in the dark for a longer while. The claim is that it will glow for up to 10 hours; I have not verified that it will last that long, but it does go for a long time, long enough in most situations that it will continue to glow long after sunset. This is really all I can ask.

The vial appears to be filled with some sort of phosphorous-coated granules. As a first test I exposed them to the bright light of an LED flashlight for about 30 seconds, and the vial glowed for several minutes afterward. It wasn’t all that bright, but I didn’t give it long to “charge” either. It was enough as a proof of concept though. It lasts longer under extended exposure to bright light such as direct sunlight.

The extra clips that come with the vial are useful for attaching it to other things without using the ring. One of the attachments is actually the same thing as a pen clip, which is useful for clipping to a tent flap, umbrella or other fabric surface.

Especially when considering the cost, this is really an easy product to recommend if you need a luminous marker. It really does work for a long while, it’s very easy to see and it is versatile.
text_fidelity_b: GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing

text_fidelity_a:
Selle Royal Premium Bike Pump with Over-Sized Gauge, Integrated Air Release, Auto Presta & Schrader Ready, 160psi, Ball/Bladder Needles Included We've got a lot of tires in this family. I used this pump on a small 8 inch electric scooter tube,18 inch kids bike tubes,16 inch beginner bike tubes, 12 inch balance bike tube and fat tubeless trike tires. It worked great on most of them.
The most challenging one is actually the electric scooter tire while it's mounted. Several other chucks fail to get proper seating on the difficult to get to valve stem. This pump got a lock with very little effort. The 16 inch tire, I had to tilt the stem since the locking lever is so long. Other than that, no problems. The 12 inch tire was actually easier.
The pump action works fairly smooth. On an 18 inch 40 PSI tire, I got an average of 5 PSIs per pump.
The hose is soft and flexible. Pretty much on the limp side. Not stiff at all. Very easy to work with.
The air release worked well. I was able to bleed out 1 PSI at a time.
The one thing I would have liked is a turn lock to hold the handle in place. I lifted this several times by the handle and the body slides down as it lifts. I guess I wouldn't mind a shorter chuck locking lever as well.
Overall, this is a lightweight effective pump that happens to work great for all of our tires. And the handle compartment is a nice little feature. It took me a few seconds of pulling to see the press tabs on the underside.

text_fidelity_a:
LuTuo Bike Pannier Bag Waterproof, 48L large Capacity Bicycle Bags for Rear Carrier, 3 in 1 Bike Rack Bag, Bike Trunk Bag Saddle Bags for Travel, Double Cycle Storage Bag for Mountain Bike Roadbike These have become my favorite bags easily. Love these. Almost all good to great aspects and only a few minor issues (very minor)

pros
Easy to attach: go on to the bike rack via hooks with no fuss, secure further with velcro straps that are long enough to be secure (not always the case with every bag I've found), backpack fits on top secured by multiple buckles so it has no movement. Every now and then (very rarely, fewer than five times in several months of use) I'll hit a particular bad bump and one sidebar hook will come off. It's happened so rarely, and to no effect (still secured by the other hook and the strap) that I haven't bothered to see if a simple tightening of the hook opening will "fix" it.

Spacious: I commute to work, shower there, and I teach, so I carry a lot: a full set of clothes (socks, underwear, pants, shirt, heavier shirt for warmth in the bldg),a 16-inch MacBook Pro, an iPad Pro, my phone, a bag of whiteboard markers, a bag of tech stuff (hub, flash drive, screen rag, etc), often a folder with some papers, and a plastic bag with rain gear (rain pants, rain jacket), a toiletry bag and deodorant. And sometimes, with the discrepancy between morning and afternoon temps, I have to toss in the long-sleeved shirt and tights I word in the morning commute. All of if fits (with one caveat below) with room to spare. I love the space. Absolutely love it.

Water-resistant: I haven't tried a downpour. But I've had a shower or two, biked on some wet gravel trails with puddles, and used my sink sprayer to test a bit as well. The bags resist water quite well and even spraying from the side at the zippers directly (thanks to positioning they're protected from rain from directly above) no water entered the bags. I can't say if that would be true for a truly sustained downpour, but I have little to no concern about the water protection. And it comes with a rain cover anyway, so with that, zero concerns

The modular system is great. When I'm running out and need hardly anything, I use one bag. When I commute to my one workday where I don't need to shower thanks to a shorter ride, I take two bags. When I do my longer commute, I take the two bags plus the backpack. It's a lot easier taking my stuff from the locker room to my classroom bldg. with a backpack than a big bag with a shoulder strap (my prior biking bag). The backpack is spacious and also water-resistant. Straps are basic and unpadded, but I don't wear it for long.

Durability: been using it nigh on daily for months and certainly no issues or concerns at all. Time will tell but looking good. Feels like good build quality.

Cons
My 16-inch MacBook Pro just barely fits in, and I have to be a bit careful with the zipper when closing. If the bags were a 1/2 wider (maybe even a 1/4), it would slip in and zipper with no concern at all. Something to think about for a future iteration.

absolutely thrilled with these. I have had some bad bags, average ones, and good ones. My last one was excellent (I've kept it as a backup), but these are more convenient in several ways, so easily my go-to choice
text_fidelity_b: LuTuo Bike Pannier Bag Waterproof, 48L large Capacity Bicycle Bags for Rear Carrier, 3 in 1 Bike Rack Bag, Bike Trunk Bag Saddle Bags for Travel, Double Cycle Storage Bag for Mountain Bike Roadbike

Hi-Seas Grand Slam Monofilament Leader I found this to be good quality leader line. Granted, I can't really tell the difference between brands, but this is just as good as any other line I've purchased. What sets this apart and made it a 5-star product are three points:

1. I could get it in 130 pound test. That's just a wee bit thicker than 100 pound, but I'm finding it to make all the difference in terms of strength and longevity. While 100, 150 and 200 pound test are not too had to find, this was the first time I was able to find 130 pound.

2. I could get a small spool (35 yards). I don't use much leader line, so while buying a big spool does cost less per foot/yard, the money is wasted when I lose the spool (which is why I had to purchase this)

3. It comes on a very nice plastic spool with an edge guard. I've uploaded a picture. I thought it would be in a plastic bag as pictured, but my order came on a spool.

Now, I just have to make sure I don't lose this one too!

text_fidelity_a: Cascade Mountain Tech Trekking Poles - Carbon Fiber Walking or Hiking Sticks with Quick Adjustable Locks These trekking poles are well worth the money.  I spent half of what others spent for poles and these outlasted all the others and were as light if not lighter than the rest.  The locking mechanism is super strong,  I weigh about 220 lbs and they never collapsed on me once.  I never had to readjust them due to slippage either.  Friends that weight closer to 150 lbs were struggling with their poles the whole trip and some even bent their aluminum poles.  By the end of the trip these things looked like hell.  Decent amount of scratches from use but I imagine they still have plenty of life left in them, I have barely even scratched the surface.  Now I should note I am not a trekking pole person, generally I don't use them so that also means I probably used these about half as much as the others used theirs. This trip kind of required them to help with the extreme boulder terrain and portions of off trail hiking up mountain passes. After buying these I would probably always bring them on trips like this.
text_fidelity_b: Cascade Mountain Tech Trekking Poles - Carbon Fiber Walking or Hiking Sticks with Quick Adjustable Locks

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Superflash USB bike tail light If you need a taillight bright enough in solid mode for foggy/rainy daytime riding, this is probably not the taillight for you.

I used the old AAA powered Superflash for many years and it was good enough for my type of riding. Mostly unlit trails. Some city riding. I always used the flash mode which is very attention grabbing. Rain, fog, snow, whatever. Solid mode is still good on a clear night, but not for low visibility daytime conditions.

The old Superflash had a tendency to pop off when riding over bumps. Also had a flimsy switch.

This model has built-in batteries which means it's one solid unit that wont fall apart. The switch is improved as well. I don't think it's really any brighter than the old one.

Cosmetically it is improved from the old model due to the black plastic housing. White plastic looks grungy after a while.

I still consider the Superflash to be a good value for the money.

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer My wife and I are "seasoned citizens" who just got back into a workout program at the local YMCA. To keep our motivation at the highest level, I thought it would be a good idea to be able to chart our progress on a regular basis -- enter two pedometers! We are also able to post our daily results online by way of a major drug store chain, so that helps with motivation as well!

Now to the pedometer:
1. to us, it is excellent in every way. It keeps track of your daily steps, it resets itself to zero at midnight, and it saves seven days' worth of results for your review;
2. it clips to your belt or pants very securely thanks to the clip into which the pedometer fits. So far we have found no need to attach the small strap that comes with the pedometer;
3. although the pedometer is "always on" once you insert the battery, that does not seem to be a problem; it takes the CR2032 battery readily available in stores;
4. the numbers are easy to read if you have "older" eyes;
5. the pedometer is a little longer than 2" -- not large at all, just the right size;
6. the pedometer keeps track of routine walking AND specific aerobic movement, such as walking on a treadmill; the total number includes the aerobic steps, but the aerobic steps are shown separately -- a nice feature.

We are very glad we have our pedometers. I think you will be very happy with this investment in your health and well-being!
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

3 different screens when you are checking your irregular heartbeat is too many, possibly very dangerous if you are checking to see if you are having real heart issues. The 3 screens (an Ad for more services), the screen of what you would like to do (record services), "which EKG device you are using 3 lead or 6, then touch to your leg.

When you open the Omron Heart Rate Monitor and press the sync button it works with the 1st screen and syncs automatically with Kardia. Why can't Kardia?

It would be great if when you opened the App and clicked the first screen you were able to take your EKG right away or at least make it as a device option for those of us that bought this due to major health issues.  Many of us are using this as a real time solution for irregular heart beat monitoring that the DR cannot catch with a conventional 24hr wearable Med device.

Ah Lastly it also asks you if you would like to upgrade to storing your results online with no way to upgrade, it doesn't upgrade.
